## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Cost & Sustainability

Assesses cost efficiency and sustainability as visible in IaC, deployment, scheduler and pipeline configuration,
using local, pinned summaries of the Azure Well-Architected Framework and Green Software Foundation guidance.

#### Inputs

IaC compute/scaling/sizing, autoscaling, storage lifecycle and retention, backup/replication, log-workspace,
policy/budget, CDN/gateway, scheduler (cron/CronJob/timer) and CI/CD pipeline files, per `compliance-inventory`.
The orchestrator marks this subject N/A when `iacFound` is false.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/azure-well-architected-cost-sustainability.md` — WAF-01…WAF-51. Always load.
- `references/standards/green-software-patterns.md` — GSP-01…GSP-23. Always load.
- `references/standards/green-software-principles.md` — GSFL-01…GSFL-04. Always load.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md` and the three standards files.
2. Every active element is generic and applies to any cloud, Kubernetes or on-premises IaC; judge each one by the
   cloud-neutral requirement, using the target's own resource types as evidence. Retired rows are not evaluated.
3. For each active check (COST-01…COST-03, COST-05…COST-10; COST-04 is retired and is not written to
   `checkResults`), evaluate only the elements it lists whose "Applies when" condition holds in the subject's files.
   If none apply, mark the check N/A with that reason (e.g. COST-08 when no backup/replication config exists;
   COST-09 when no region, CDN, compression or schedule settings are in scope).
4. Evidence rule: fail an element only on concrete evidence in the files (e.g. a fixed high SKU with N instances and
   no autoscaler or recorded justification; a storage account with no lifecycle rule; a log workspace with no
   retention). Don't fail on assumed demand. Use confidence `medium` unless the evidence is unambiguous.
5. Excess only (COST-08): fail backup retention, replication or DR capacity only when it **exceeds** the
   requirements stated in the repo (tier, SLO, RTO, RPO, retention rule). Never fail it for being insufficient or
   missing — that is assessed by `review-disaster-recovery`. If no requirement is stated, don't judge proportionality
   ("no stated recovery target to judge against"); only the cheaper-tier placement of long-term backups (WAF-36) can
   still be evaluated.
6. Severity: every element's level is REVIEW, so each Finding takes the check's default severity from
   `checklist.md`; `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is always that default.
7. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `WAF-01`); the report script derives `standard` and `url`
   from it, so don't write them.
8. Boundaries: **owned here** — autoscale maximums, over-provisioning, data archive and purge; excess backup/DR
   capacity (COST-08, see step 5); telemetry volume and over-retention. **Don't fail for** too few instances or
   zones, or too little redundancy (review-reliability AZRL-27/48; this skill fails only *excess*); missing or
   insufficient backup or DR (review-disaster-recovery; see step 5); caching, compression, async I/O or offloading in
   code (review-performance; WAF-41/42 judge only CDN/gateway config); missing logging coverage or retention below a
   requirement (review-monitoring step 6, review-observability; this skill judges only excess volume and
   over-retention, WAF-32/33); whether security inspection hops exist (security skills; WAF-45 judges only their
   cost); load or performance tests (review-testing TST-12).

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

## File: `references/standards/azure-well-architected-cost-sustainability.md`

*Load rule: WAF-01…WAF-51. Always load.*

### Azure Well-Architected Framework — Cost Optimization & Sustainability — localized summary

- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (the source uses no normative keywords); severity is the owning check's default.
- Scope column: G = generic (any cloud / Kubernetes). Every element is Scope G; the only Azure-only element (WAF-51) was generalized on 2026-11-12. Azure product names appear only as examples.
- CO column: the WAF Cost Optimization checklist code the element implements (traceability only).

#### COST-01 — Right-sizing and tier selection

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-01 | REVIEW | G | Size compute (instance count, vCPU/memory, SKU) to measured or stated demand. A large fixed SKU needs a recorded justification. | compute in IaC | CO:07 |
| WAF-02 | REVIEW | G | Pick service tiers for features actually used. A higher tier chosen only for unused features is waste. | PaaS tiers | CO:07 |
| WAF-03 | REVIEW | G | Disable paid platform features and add-ons that aren't used. | PaaS options | CO:07 |
| WAF-04 | REVIEW | G | Availability and performance settings (zone redundancy, replica count, premium storage, SLA tier) match stated requirements, no more. | compute, storage | CO:07 |
| WAF-05 | REVIEW | G | Use current SKU/service generations and keep platforms, runtimes and OS images current. | compute | CO:07 |
| WAF-06 | REVIEW | G | Avoid dedicated or isolated infrastructure (dedicated hosts, isolated tiers) unless requirements justify it. | compute | CO:07 |
| WAF-07 | REVIEW | G | Size and tier each flow by its priority. Low-priority flows get cheaper tiers, and dissimilar flows aren't forced onto one oversized resource. | multiple components | CO:09 |
| WAF-08 | REVIEW | G | Capacity per region follows the share of users each region serves. Low-traffic regions don't mirror the main region's capacity. | multi-region | CO:08 |

#### COST-02 — Autoscaling

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-09 | REVIEW | G | Autoscale variable-load components against observed demand instead of running a fixed, peak-sized deployment. | scalable compute | CO:12 |
| WAF-10 | REVIEW | G | Rules scale in as well as out: scale out at the last responsible moment and scale in as soon as practical. | autoscaler | CO:12 |
| WAF-11 | REVIEW | G | Scale on workload-relevant metrics (sustained CPU, queue length, traffic), with a cooldown or stabilization window so short spikes don't cause churn. | autoscaler | CO:12 |
| WAF-12 | REVIEW | G | Every autoscaler has a tested maximum, and non-prod maximums are lower than production. | autoscaler | CO:04 |
| WAF-13 | REVIEW | G | Queue and event workers scale on event count or queue depth (e.g. KEDA), down to zero where possible. | queue/event workers | CO:12 |

#### COST-03 — Environments and idle resources

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-14 | REVIEW | G | Non-prod environments shut down, scale to zero or run on a schedule outside working hours. | non-prod env | CO:08 |
| WAF-15 | REVIEW | G | Non-prod uses lower tiers, fewer instances and lower scaling limits through per-environment parameters, while keeping the same services, OS and CPU architecture as production. | non-prod env | CO:08 |
| WAF-16 | REVIEW | G | Non-prod isn't an exact replica of production: no geo-replication, zone redundancy or premium options unless a test needs them. | non-prod env | CO:08 |
| WAF-17 | REVIEW | G | Short-lived dev, test and preview environments are created on demand and destroyed after use. | non-prod env | CO:04 |
| WAF-18 | REVIEW | G | Keep preproduction environments few. Combine environments whose functions don't overlap. | non-prod env | CO:08 |
| WAF-19 | REVIEW | G | No orphaned or unused resources (unattached disks/IPs, empty plans, leftover proof-of-concept resources). Lifecycle tooling removes child resources with their parent. | any IaC | CO:07 |
| WAF-20 | REVIEW | G | Non-prod has shorter log/data retention and less frequent backups than production. | non-prod env | CO:08 |

#### COST-05 — Cost allocation metadata

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-21 | REVIEW | G | Apply consistent cost metadata (tags/labels for workload, environment, cost center or feature) to every resource, e.g. from a shared tag map. | any IaC | CO:03 |
| WAF-22 | REVIEW | G | Every resource has an identifiable owner (owner tag, or ownership documented for the resource group or stack). | any IaC | CO:03 |
| WAF-23 | REVIEW | G | Tagging is enforced or inherited automatically (policy, tag inheritance, provider default tags), not left to convention. | policy/provider config | CO:04 |

#### COST-06 — Spending guardrails and targets

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-24 | REVIEW | G | Budgets with actual-cost and forecast-cost alerts at defined thresholds exist, preferably defined as code. | any IaC | CO:03, CO:04 |
| WAF-25 | REVIEW | G | Cost anomaly alerts are configured. | any IaC | CO:03 |
| WAF-26 | REVIEW | G | Policies restrict allowed resource types, SKUs and regions, at least for non-prod. | policy IaC | CO:04 |
| WAF-27 | REVIEW | G | IaC pipelines estimate cost before deploying and gate releases on it. | pipeline files | CO:04 |
| WAF-28 | REVIEW | G | A cost estimate (cost model) and budget for the workload is documented in the repo. | docs | CO:02 |
| WAF-29 | REVIEW | G | Efficiency or carbon baselines and targets are defined (e.g. cost per transaction, carbon score, CPU/memory baselines used as pipeline quality gates). | docs, pipeline files | CO:03 |

#### COST-07 — Data lifecycle, retention and telemetry volume

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-30 | REVIEW | G | Storage access tiers match how often the data is read (hot / cool / cold / archive). | storage | CO:10 |
| WAF-31 | REVIEW | G | Lifecycle rules move data to cheaper tiers and delete it at the end of its retention period. | storage | CO:10 |
| WAF-32 | REVIEW | G | Log and telemetry stores have an explicit, bounded retention period. | log workspaces, diagnostics | CO:10 |
| WAF-33 | REVIEW | G | Telemetry volume is controlled: sampling, ingestion filters/transformations, only needed signals, and no verbose production log level by default. | log/telemetry config | CO:10 |
| WAF-34 | REVIEW | G | Compress stored data and use efficient formats (e.g. columnar for analytics) where the tradeoff is favorable. | storage, data pipelines | CO:10 |
| WAF-35 | REVIEW | G | Don't duplicate datasets across services or stores without a clear reason. | multiple data stores | CO:10 |

#### COST-08 — Proportionate backup and redundancy

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-36 | REVIEW | G | Backup retention, frequency and type (incremental where possible) match stated business or compliance needs. Long-term backups go to cheaper tiers. | backup config | CO:10 |
| WAF-37 | REVIEW | G | Replication and redundancy (local / zone / geo, multi-region) match how critical the data or system is. Multi-region only where required. | storage, multi-region | CO:10 |
| WAF-38 | REVIEW | G | A DR environment is sized to its RTO/RPO (cold, warm, or redeploy via IaC) instead of mirroring peak production. | DR IaC | CO:08 |

#### COST-09 — Placement, data transfer and timing

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-39 | REVIEW | G | Keep dependent resources in the same region. Avoid cross-region routing or replication that no workload need justifies. | multi-resource | CO:10 |
| WAF-40 | REVIEW | G | Place workloads near users when the traffic pattern justifies it. | region choice | CO:10 |
| WAF-41 | REVIEW | G | Serve frequently requested static content from a CDN, edge cache or static hosting, with tuned cache TTLs. | static content | CO:12 |
| WAF-42 | REVIEW | G | Compress payloads in transit (gateway, CDN or app compression; compact serialization). | HTTP endpoints | CO:11 |
| WAF-43 | REVIEW | G | Weigh carbon intensity alongside cost, latency and resiliency when choosing regions. | region choice | — |
| WAF-44 | REVIEW | G | Schedule flexible batch jobs in lower-carbon or lower-cost windows, not on fixed convenience schedules. | batch/cron schedules | — |
| WAF-45 | REVIEW | G | Don't route traffic through central inspection hubs or extra hops it doesn't need. | network IaC | — |

#### COST-10 — Platform choice, consolidation and pricing model

| ID | Level | Scope | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAF-46 | REVIEW | G | Prefer PaaS, serverless or containers to self-managed VMs where they fit the workload. | compute, databases | CO:07 |
| WAF-47 | REVIEW | G | Consolidate compatible components onto shared hosting (plans, clusters, database pools, gateways) to raise density, while respecting isolation needs. | multiple components | CO:14 |
| WAF-48 | REVIEW | G | Reuse central shared services (log workspace, firewall, gateway) instead of deploying duplicates per workload. | platform IaC | CO:14 |
| WAF-49 | REVIEW | G | Use spot or preemptible capacity only for work that tolerates interruption, and handle eviction. | compute | CO:05 |
| WAF-50 | REVIEW | G | Billing model fits usage: consumption pricing for ephemeral or variable use, commitments only for steady permanent components, and usage aligned with billing increments. | compute | CO:05, CO:06 |
| WAF-51 | REVIEW | G | Apply the licensing benefits and non-production pricing the provider offers where licenses and environments allow (bring-your-own-license, dev/test pricing; e.g. Azure Hybrid Benefit `licenseType`, AWS `license_model = "bring-your-own-license"`). | licensed VMs or databases in IaC | CO:05 |

## File: `references/standards/green-software-patterns.md`

*Load rule: GSP-01…GSP-23. Always load.*

### Green Software Patterns — localized summary

- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (the source uses no normative keywords); severity is the owning check's default.

| ID | Level | Pattern (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSP-01 | REVIEW | Rightsize VMs to their observed utilization (vCPU/memory). | VMs | COST-01 |
| GSP-02 | REVIEW | Pick the pre-configured server size that best matches the process's utilization. | VMs / node pools | COST-01 |
| GSP-03 | REVIEW | Evaluate non-x86 CPU architectures (e.g. Arm) for energy efficiency and performance. | compute SKUs | COST-01 |
| GSP-04 | REVIEW | Drive average CPU utilization to an optimal level. Autoscale targets aren't set so low that instances sit idle. | autoscaler | COST-02 |
| GSP-05 | REVIEW | Scale infrastructure with user load, scaling back in periods of low or no activity. | autoscaler | COST-02 |
| GSP-06 | REVIEW | Scale Kubernetes workloads on relevant demand metrics (e.g. KEDA), down to zero when idle. | Kubernetes | COST-02 |
| GSP-07 | REVIEW | Scale logical components independently instead of scaling the whole application. | multi-component | COST-02 |
| GSP-08 | REVIEW | Keep components stateless (state externalized) so they can run small and scale freely. | app hosting config | COST-02 |
| GSP-09 | REVIEW | Scale down applications and hardware that aren't in use, on a schedule. | non-prod / idle apps | COST-03 |
| GSP-10 | REVIEW | Scale Kubernetes Deployments/StatefulSets to zero outside working hours. | Kubernetes non-prod | COST-03 |
| GSP-11 | REVIEW | Minimize the total number of deployed environments. | environments | COST-03 |
| GSP-12 | REVIEW | Decommission unused assets. Consolidate sparsely used instances (e.g. small databases) into one. | any IaC | COST-03 |
| GSP-13 | REVIEW | Delete unused storage resources. | storage | COST-07 |
| GSP-14 | REVIEW | Set retention policies on storage so unused data is deleted automatically. | storage | COST-07 |
| GSP-15 | REVIEW | Move data off underutilized storage resources and consolidate. | storage | COST-07 |
| GSP-16 | REVIEW | Compress stored data with a tool suited to each use case. | storage | COST-07 |
| GSP-17 | REVIEW | Match service-level objectives (and the redundancy built for them) to what users actually need. | redundancy config | COST-08 |
| GSP-18 | REVIEW | Choose the region closest to where most network traffic goes. | region choice | COST-09 |
| GSP-19 | REVIEW | Cache static data (images, audio) instead of re-transferring it. | static content | COST-09 |
| GSP-20 | REVIEW | Compress transmitted data, and enable all supported text-compression formats on the server. | HTTP endpoints | COST-09 |
| GSP-21 | REVIEW | Time-shift recurring jobs (e.g. Kubernetes CronJobs) using carbon-intensity forecasts. | batch/cron | COST-09 |
| GSP-22 | REVIEW | Containerize workloads with minimal dependencies. | compute | COST-10 |
| GSP-23 | REVIEW | Use serverless services where requirements allow. | compute | COST-10 |

## File: `references/standards/green-software-principles.md`

*Load rule: GSFL-01…GSFL-04. Always load.*

### Green Software Foundation — Principles of Green Software Engineering — localized summary

- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (the source uses no normative keywords); severity is the owning check's default.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSFL-01 | REVIEW | Demand shifting: run time- or location-flexible work when and where grid carbon intensity is lower. | batch/cron, region choice | COST-09 |
| GSFL-02 | REVIEW | Energy proportionality: run fewer, well-used servers instead of many lightly loaded ones. | compute | COST-10 |
| GSFL-03 | REVIEW | Hardware efficiency: raise device utilization through shared cloud capacity and consolidation, and avoid hardware provisioned for rare peaks. | compute | COST-10 |
| GSFL-04 | REVIEW | Measure with a rate-based metric such as the Software Carbon Intensity (SCI = ((E × I) + M) per R), not only totals. | docs | COST-06 |
